text:
You will need to make sure that your husband doesn't need a visa for Jordan with his foreign passport, as he won't be able to get the benefit of Israeli visa-free arrangement without the Israeli passport. 

Also, Israeli citizens normally have to enter Israel with an Israeli passport, but there is a current relaxation of the rule (https://www.gov.il/en/pages/news-exit-with-foriegn-passport-300926). However, if your husband doesn't have a current visa in his passport, the normal expectation would be that he have an ETA. The interesting issue is that I understand he isn't from an ETA eligible country (as Turkish citizens normally require a visa). If you are going to be reentering Israel through a land border, it may be less of an issue (as an ETA is needed to board a flight) - but I would recommend bringing a copy of the citizenship certificate and ID card at least to show that he is actually Israeli.
